> **New Concept: Quasi-Primitive Modules**
> We are introducing a new constraint. A module is **quasi-primitive** if, roughly speaking, it stays "mostly together" when restricted to any normal subgroup. Specifically, when you look at how a normal subgroup acts on $V$, the space doesn't shatter into many unrelated pieces; it remains homogeneous (composed of copies of a single irreducible type).
>
> **Why make this assumption?**
> Just like before, we are using a reduction argument. If $V$ were *not* quasi-primitive, it would break apart in a specific, structured way when restricted to a normal subgroup. We will show that this "breaking apart" actually helps us prove the theorem using induction. Therefore, the only hard case left is when $V$ *is* quasi-primitive.
